status: Published practice plan and daily briefs; detailed lesson PDFs and solved implementations are not included.

sessions.implementation: Implement push, pop, peek and empty on a buffer; double capacity when full. Pop does not shrink.
sessions.application: Trace and implement a LIFO operation log; preview nesting as an application.
sessions.invariant: The live prefix is exactly the stack, and its final entry is the top.
sessions.complexity: Push: O(1) amortized, O(n) on a resize; pop/peek O(1). Capacity is O(n) for insertion-only growth; after many pops it tracks historical maximum size.
sessions.edge_cases: Empty pop, singleton, duplicates, several growth boundaries.
sessions.gate_drill: GATE DA 2024 Q16: match ADTs to operations; compare single-operation and sequence costs. Full resizing accounting returns later.

sessions.implementation: Implement a fixed-capacity ring queue with head and size; derive tail=(head+size)%capacity.
sessions.application: Replay FIFO requests in a ring buffer; trace both-end deque operations without requiring a second full implementation.
sessions.invariant: Logical item i lives at (head+i)%capacity; 0<=size<=capacity.
sessions.complexity: O(1) worst-case endpoint operations, O(capacity) allocated storage; no list.pop(0).
sessions.edge_cases: Full vs empty, wrap-around, capacity one, invalid operation contract.
sessions.gate_drill: GATE DA 2024 Q32: deque trace; compare FIFO with LIFO.

sessions.implementation: Implement Node, traversal, prepend, append with tail and one deletion case; finish empty/head/tail cases during the operation-log block. Preview doubly linked representation.
sessions.application: Replay insert/delete operations on a singly linked list; diagram the extra prev links in a doubly linked list.
sessions.invariant: Every live node is reachable exactly once; tail.next is None; empty head and tail agree.
sessions.complexity: Search/delete by value O(n); prepend and append with tail O(1); deleting a known node still needs its predecessor in a singly linked list.
sessions.edge_cases: Empty list, deleting head/tail, one node, missing key.
sessions.gate_drill: GATE DA 2025 Q27: explain why a sorted linked list lacks constant-time midpoint access.

sessions.implementation: Implement an integer-key map with buckets: put/get/delete; force collisions using key modulo bucket count.
sessions.application: Replay put/get/update/delete on a chained integer-key map, including collisions; preview membership and counting applications.
sessions.invariant: Each key belongs to its hash bucket and appears at most once; updates replace its value.
sessions.complexity: Expected O(1) map operations with suitable hashing and bounded load; O(n) worst case; application expected O(n) time and O(n) space.
sessions.edge_cases: Colliding keys, duplicate update, absent deletion, negative integer keys under Python modulo.
sessions.gate_drill: Original collision and load-factor trace; distinguish expected lookup bounds from worst-case collisions.

sessions.implementation: Implement sift_up, sift_down, push, peek and pop in a zero-indexed array; do not call heapq yet.
sessions.application: Replay min-priority requests with push/pop; contrast FIFO order, sorted order and heap order.
sessions.invariant: Every parent is <= its children; after a local repair only the repair path may temporarily violate heap order.
sessions.complexity: O(log n) comparisons/moves per push/pop; peek O(1). Dynamic-array resizing makes push O(log n) amortized overall, with occasional O(n) allocation work.
sessions.edge_cases: Empty pop, one child, equal priorities, ascending/reversed inserts.
sessions.gate_drill: Original heap-array MSQ; end the week by choosing between all five structures for five small tasks.

sessions.implementation: Reuse Day 1 stack; implement a bracket validator without counting alone.
sessions.application: Validate mixed nested brackets; optional transfer: evaluate a postfix expression.
sessions.invariant: The stack contains unmatched openings in encounter order.
sessions.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) worst-case auxiliary space.
sessions.edge_cases: Early closing, wrong nesting, unmatched opening; empty input is accepted in our local variant.
sessions.gate_drill: Original MCQ: why equal counts do not imply correct nesting; trace maximum active stack depth.

sessions.implementation: Implement unresolved-index stack with explicit strict-greater comparisons.
sessions.application: For every array position, return the index of its next strictly greater value, or -1.
sessions.invariant: Stack indices increase; their values are non-increasing; popped indices receive their first greater successor.
sessions.complexity: O(n) aggregate time: each index is pushed once and popped at most once; O(n) space.
sessions.edge_cases: Increasing, decreasing, all equal, repeated peaks.
sessions.gate_drill: Original NAT: count pushes/pops on a decreasing then increasing sequence; distinguish nested loops from quadratic work.

sessions.focus: Queue applications: lazy transfer and amortization
sessions.implementation: Implement lazy transfer only when the output stack is empty.
sessions.application: Build a FIFO queue using two stacks and replay a long burst followed by alternating operations.
sessions.invariant: Reading output top-to-bottom followed by input bottom-to-top gives FIFO order.
sessions.complexity: An individual dequeue can be O(n); total O(m) stack primitives over m operations, O(1) amortized per operation; O(n) stored items.
sessions.edge_cases: Transfer after peek, repeated peek, enqueue after partial drain, empty behavior.
sessions.gate_drill: Original potential/aggregate analysis MCQ; GATE DA 2026 Q39: compare total call count with maximum active depth.

sessions.implementation: Implement iterative reversal with prev, curr and saved next.
sessions.application: Reverse a singly linked list in place; optional transfer: reverse a specified prefix.
sessions.invariant: prev is the reversed processed prefix; curr starts the untouched suffix; their nodes partition the original list.
sessions.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space; no recursive call stack.
sessions.edge_cases: Empty, singleton, two nodes; verify no node loss, duplication or cycle.
sessions.gate_drill: Original pointer-state MSQ: identify which update order loses the suffix.

sessions.implementation: Build a dummy-head merge and reconnect existing nodes.
sessions.application: Merge two sorted linked lists without allocating a node for every output entry.
sessions.invariant: The output prefix is sorted and complete for all consumed nodes; both remaining suffixes stay sorted.
sessions.complexity: O(n+m) time, O(1) auxiliary space when reusing nodes, excluding a constant dummy node.
sessions.edge_cases: One empty input, equal values, uneven lengths, tail attachment; inputs are disjoint acyclic lists.
sessions.gate_drill: Original MCQ: stability with ties and the cost of finding an insertion position.

sessions.implementation: Implement cycle detection; trace positions before writing the loop condition.
sessions.application: Determine whether a linked list contains a cycle; optional: locate its entry after deriving the meeting argument.
sessions.invariant: Fast and slow traverse the same successor relation at different speeds; in a cycle their relative position advances modulo cycle length.
sessions.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space, where n counts distinct reachable nodes.
sessions.edge_cases: No cycle, self-loop, two-node cycle, long stem, cycle at head.
sessions.gate_drill: Original NAT: number of advances before a meeting; distinguish middle-finding from cycle-detection contracts.

sessions.focus: Hash maps for lookup and counting
sessions.implementation: Implement a complement lookup; optional frequency-map variation.
sessions.application: Find two distinct indices whose values sum to a target without sorting.
sessions.invariant: Before processing index i, the map contains usable indices strictly before i.
sessions.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) space under hashing assumptions; pathological lookup can make total O(n^2).
sessions.edge_cases: Duplicate values, same value needed twice, no pair, negative values.
sessions.gate_drill: Original MSQ: lookup before insert vs insert before lookup; compare sorting-plus-two-pointers.

sessions.implementation: Implement linear probing with EMPTY/OCCUPIED/DELETED states; bound a probe by table capacity.
sessions.application: Repair lookup after deleting a colliding key; optional transfer: rehash a small table into doubled capacity.
sessions.invariant: Only EMPTY terminates an unsuccessful search; DELETED preserves the probe chain.
sessions.complexity: O(1) expected operations only with appropriate hashing and controlled load/tombstones; O(n) worst case. A rebuild costs O(n) expected under the same assumptions.
sessions.edge_cases: Delete middle of cluster, wrap-around, full table, updating a key beyond a tombstone.
sessions.gate_drill: GATE DA 2025 Q18: linear probing; GATE DA 2024 Q21: state the uniform-hashing assumption.

sessions.implementation: Implement counts of prior prefix sums, initialized with zero seen once.
sessions.application: Count contiguous subarrays with sum K, allowing negative values.
sessions.invariant: Before the current prefix is inserted, counts describe all earlier prefix sums; their difference identifies a valid subarray.
sessions.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) space under hashing assumptions.
sessions.edge_cases: K=0, all zeroes, negatives, repeated prefix sums; ask why a positive-only sliding window fails.
sessions.gate_drill: Original NAT: hand-trace prefix counts and count occurrences rather than distinct prefix values.

sessions.focus: Killer application: linked list + hashing for LRU
sessions.implementation: Using a provided sentinel-node scaffold, implement detach and append-to-recent; then combine them with a key-to-node map for get/put. Do not use OrderedDict.
sessions.application: Implement bounded least-recently-used caching with positive capacity. The linked-list primitive lab and cache integration share this session’s coding budget; a working scaffold is allowed.
sessions.invariant: Map keys equal list keys; each key has one node; list order is recency; size never exceeds capacity after an operation.
sessions.complexity: Expected O(1) get/put with hash-map assumptions and O(capacity) storage; worst-case hash lookup is not O(1).
sessions.edge_cases: Capacity one, update existing key, get changes recency, eviction, missing get.
sessions.gate_drill: Original cache-state trace; prove reciprocal links and map/list agreement, then explain expected O(1) get/put.

sessions.implementation: Extend Day 5 sifts with bottom-up heapify; adapt comparison for an in-place max-heapsort.
sessions.application: Sort an array by moving the maximum to a growing sorted suffix and repairing the reduced heap.
sessions.invariant: Active prefix is a max-heap; suffix is sorted and contains the removed maxima.
sessions.complexity: Heapify O(n) via node-height counting; heapsort O(n log n), O(1) auxiliary space with iterative sifts; normally unstable.
sessions.edge_cases: Duplicates, already sorted, reverse sorted, empty, one element.
sessions.gate_drill: Original NAT: compare n repeated insertions with bottom-up heapify and justify the height-sum bound.

sessions.focus: Killer application: top-k in a stream
sessions.implementation: Maintain a size-k min-heap using Day 5 operations; heapq is permitted after the foundational implementation.
sessions.application: Maintain the kth largest observation as values arrive, counting duplicate observations.
sessions.invariant: Once k values exist, the heap contains k largest values seen; its root is the kth largest.
sessions.complexity: O(log k) accepted update, O(1) rejected comparison/peek; O(n log(k+1)) total upper bound and O(k) storage.
sessions.edge_cases: k=1, fewer than k values, duplicates, negatives, a long rejected tail.
sessions.gate_drill: Original MCQ: why a min-heap, not a max-heap, is the correct retained frontier.

sessions.implementation: Keep one unconsumed head per nonempty sorted source in a heap; include a source tie-breaker.
sessions.application: Merge k sorted arrays or iterators; optional: return a lazy iterator instead of a materialized result.
sessions.invariant: The heap contains the smallest unconsumed candidate from every unfinished source.
sessions.complexity: O(k+N log(k+1)) time including source setup; O(k) auxiliary heap space, plus O(N) output if materialized.
sessions.edge_cases: Empty sources, all sources empty, equal values from different sources, uneven source lengths.
sessions.gate_drill: Original NAT: bound heap size and distinguish auxiliary space from returned output.

sessions.implementation: Build a deque of candidate indices; expire old indices and remove dominated values before appending.
sessions.application: Return the maximum for every consecutive window of k values without rescanning the window.
sessions.invariant: Candidate indices increase and their values decrease; all retained indices lie in the current window; the front is its maximum.
sessions.complexity: O(n) aggregate time: each index is appended once and removed at most once; O(k) auxiliary deque space, plus O(n-k+1) output.
sessions.edge_cases: k=1, k=n, equal values, increasing/decreasing sequences, maximum expiring; require 1<=k<=n.
sessions.gate_drill: Original NAT: count removals and distinguish amortized per-update work from worst-case work in a single update.

sessions.implementation: Select a structure before coding; state a brute-force baseline and why it wastes work.
sessions.application: Near-transfer mock: merge k sorted linked lists by reusing nodes; optional fallback: implement FIFO using two stacks from memory.
sessions.invariant: One frontier per unfinished list; consumed nodes form the sorted output; tie-breakers avoid comparing Node objects.
sessions.complexity: O(k+N log(k+1)) time, O(k) auxiliary heap space when relinking nodes; account for initialization and empty lists.
sessions.edge_cases: Equal node values, empty list collection, disjoint lists, one source; no cycles.
sessions.gate_drill: Timed original mixed MCQ/MSQ/NAT set plus an explanation of one average/worst/amortized distinction.

organization: Week 1 introduces all five structures; Weeks 2–4 deepen applications and analysis.
